federation.desc_no_federation_partnerships_have_bee: You haven't partnered with any other timebanks yet. Browse the partner directory to find communities to connect with.

federation.federation_settings_desc: Decide whether this community can partner with other timebanks, who can send you partnership requests, and how many partners you can have.

federation.webhooks_events_required: At least one event type must be selected
federation.webhooks_secret_warning: Store this secret securely — it will not be shown again
federation.webhooks_url_hint: The endpoint URL that will receive webhook events
federation.api_doc_api_key_desc: Bearer-token access for partner API calls.
federation.api_doc_api_key_instructions: Include your API key in the Authorization header as a Bearer token. Keys can be created and managed on the API Keys page.
federation.api_doc_api_key_plain_intro: An API key is a very long password. When you federate with another timebank, you give them an API key and they give you one. Whenever their platform needs to ask yours a question, it sends the key along so yours knows the request is genuine.
federation.api_doc_api_key_plain_scope: Keys are revocable and scoped, so you can revoke access or limit a key to read-only permissions.
federation.api_doc_api_key_scopes: Each key has scoped permissions (e.g. timebanks:read, messages:write). Requests requiring a scope your key does not have will return 403 Forbidden.
federation.api_doc_error_bad_request_desc: The request body is malformed or missing required fields. Check the validation error message for details.
federation.api_doc_error_conflict_desc: The request conflicts with the current state, such as a duplicate transaction or existing opt-in.
federation.api_doc_error_forbidden_desc: Your API key does not have the required permission scope, or the target resource is restricted.
federation.api_doc_error_format_intro: All error responses follow a consistent JSON format:
federation.api_doc_error_internal_desc: An unexpected error occurred. Contact support if the issue persists.
federation.api_doc_error_not_found_desc: The requested resource does not exist, or the member or listing is not accessible via federation.
federation.api_doc_error_rate_limited_desc: Too many requests. Check the rate-limit reset header for when to retry.
federation.api_doc_error_unauthorized_desc: Missing, invalid, or expired authentication credentials. Ensure your API key or JWT is valid.
federation.api_doc_example_api_key: Example: reading data with an API key
federation.api_doc_example_message: Example: sending a message to a partner member
federation.api_doc_hmac_desc: Request signatures for tamper-resistant partner calls.
federation.api_doc_header_nonce_desc: Unique random string per request. Prevents replay attacks.
federation.api_doc_header_platform_id_desc: Your platform identifier, taken from the key prefix of your API key.
federation.api_doc_header_signature_desc: HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of the string to sign using your API secret.
federation.api_doc_header_timestamp_desc: Unix timestamp in seconds. Requests older than 5 minutes are rejected.
federation.api_doc_hmac_instructions: Sign every request using your API secret. The signature proves the request has not been tampered with in transit.
federation.api_doc_jwt_desc: Short-lived token access for server-to-server integrations.
federation.api_doc_jwt_instructions: Exchange your API key for a short-lived JWT via the token endpoint. Include it as a Bearer token. JWTs expire after 1 hour.
federation.api_doc_payload_format_desc: Every webhook delivery includes these standard fields:
federation.api_doc_rate_limit_instructions: All API responses include rate-limit headers. When the limit is exceeded, responses return 429 Too Many Requests.
federation.api_doc_rate_limit_limit_desc: Maximum requests per window, defaulting to 60 per minute.
federation.api_doc_rate_limit_remaining_desc: Requests remaining in the current window.
federation.api_doc_rate_limit_reset_desc: Unix timestamp when the window resets.
federation.api_doc_signature_verification_desc: Every webhook delivery is signed with your webhook secret using HMAC-SHA256. Verify the signature to ensure the payload is authentic and has not been tampered with. The signature is sent in the
federation.api_doc_string_to_sign_desc: Concatenate the HTTP method, full URL path, Unix timestamp, and raw request body. Use an empty string for GET requests with no body, and separate each part with a newline character.
federation.api_doc_webhook_events_desc: Everything that can trigger an automatic notification to a partner system.
federation.api_doc_webhook_delivery_intro: Webhooks are sent as POST requests to your configured HTTPS endpoint. Configure webhooks on the
federation.api_doc_webhook_event_connection_request: A cross-timebank connection request was sent
federation.api_doc_webhook_event_listing_shared: A listing was shared to the federation network
federation.api_doc_webhook_event_member_opted_in: A member opted in to federation
federation.api_doc_webhook_event_member_opted_out: A member opted out of federation
federation.api_doc_webhook_event_message_received: A federated message was received by a member in your timebank
federation.api_doc_webhook_event_message_sent: A federated message was sent from your timebank
federation.api_doc_webhook_event_partnership_reques: A new partnership request was sent to your timebank
federation.api_doc_webhook_event_transaction_comple: A time credit transaction was completed
federation.api_doc_webhook_event_transaction_create: A time credit transaction was initiated
federation.api_doc_webhook_plain_intro: A webhook is a notification sent when something happens on your side that the other side needs to know about right away, such as a cancelled transfer or a new message.
federation.api_doc_webhook_signed: Every webhook is signed. Forgeries are rejected automatically.
federation.api_doc_federation_agreement: Both sides must agree before the bridge opens, and either side can close it at any time.
federation.api_doc_federation_intro: Federation lets your timebank talk to another timebank. Once the connection is open, members can send time credits, message each other, see each other's listings, and leave reviews across the bridge.
federation.api_doc_overview_title: Start here - federation in plain English
federation.api_doc_rule_of_thumb: Rule of thumb: API keys handle requests you make on purpose. Webhooks handle surprises you need to know about without asking.
federation.api_doc_safeguard_duplicate_webhook: Unique IDs and nonces. Duplicates are ignored.
federation.api_doc_safeguard_fake_webhook: Every webhook is signed. Fakes are rejected automatically.
federation.api_doc_safeguard_global_trust: A platform-wide kill switch in super-admin disables federation everywhere instantly.
federation.api_doc_safeguard_partner_down: Queued delivery with retries. Circuit breakers stop repeated calls to an offline partner.
federation.api_doc_safeguard_partner_misbehaves: Per-partner rate limits, per-feature kill switches, and one-click suspension.
federation.api_doc_safeguard_stolen_key: Revoke in one click. Create a new key in seconds.
federation.api_doc_safeguards_title: What could go wrong? (and what we do about it)
federation.api_doc_scenario_receiving_messages: Receiving messages from the other side
federation.api_doc_scenario_transfer_cancelled: Being told a transfer you sent was cancelled

federation.api_doc_setup_step_features: Turn on the features you want to share, starting with the safest options.
federation.api_doc_setup_step_handshake: Test the handshake. One click sends a test request, and green means it is working.
federation.api_doc_setup_step_keys: Exchange API keys. Paste theirs into External Protocol Partners and keep yours safe.
federation.api_doc_setup_step_partner: Find a partner running compatible federation software.
federation.api_doc_setup_step_webhooks: Exchange webhook URLs if you want real-time events.
federation.api_doc_setup_title: How do I set up a connection? (6 steps)
federation.api_doc_summary_body: Federation is two timebanks agreeing to act as one network. API keys let them ask each other questions. Webhooks notify the other side when something urgent happens. Everything is signed, revocable, and off by default until both sides say yes.
federation.api_doc_technical_tabs_hint: Ready for the technical detail? Use the other tabs above: Authentication, Endpoints, Examples, Error codes, and Webhooks.
federation.api_doc_worry_fake_webhook: A partner sends a fake webhook
federation.api_doc_worry_global_trust: We lose trust in federation entirely
federation.api_doc_worry_partner_misbehaves: A partner misbehaves with spam or fraud

federation.rotate_secret_confirm_body: A new signing key is created immediately and the old one stops working. Partner timebanks that check your shared statistics will see errors until you give them the new key. The old key cannot be recovered.

federation.api_doc_endpoint_post_oauth_token_descri: Exchange API credentials for a JWT bearer token. Uses OAuth2 client_credentials grant. Authenticate with HTTP Basic auth where client_id is the API key prefix and client_secret is the full API key.
federation.api_doc_endpoint_post_oauth_token_param_: Space-separated list of requested scopes (e.g. "members:read listings:read")
federation.api_doc_endpoint_get_root_description: Returns API version info and a list of available endpoints. Useful as a health check.
federation.api_doc_endpoint_get_timebanks_descripti: List all partner timebanks with active partnerships. Returns name, location, member count, and partnership status.
federation.api_doc_endpoint_get_members_description: Search federated members across partner timebanks. Supports full-text search, filtering by skills, location, and timebank.
federation.api_doc_endpoint_get_members_id_descript: Get detailed profile for a single federated member, including messaging and transaction preferences.
federation.api_doc_endpoint_get_listings_descriptio: Search federated listings (offers and requests) across partner timebanks.
federation.api_doc_endpoint_get_listings_id_descrip: Get detailed information for a single federated listing.
federation.api_doc_endpoint_post_messages_descripti: Send a federated message to a member in a partner timebank. The sender must belong to your tenant.
federation.api_doc_endpoint_post_messages_param_sen: Sender user ID (must belong to your tenant)
federation.api_doc_endpoint_post_transactions_descr: Create a time credit transfer between members of partner timebanks. Requires an active credit agreement between tenants and sufficient sender balance.
federation.api_doc_endpoint_post_transactions_param: Sender user ID (must belong to your tenant)
federation.api_doc_endpoint_get_messages_descriptio: Retrieve federated messages involving your tenant. Supports filtering by direction (inbound/outbound) and a since timestamp for incremental syncing.
federation.api_doc_endpoint_get_messages_param_sinc: ISO 8601 timestamp -- only return messages after this time
federation.api_doc_endpoint_post_reviews_descriptio: Create a federated review for a member in a partner timebank. The reviewer must belong to your tenant and the reviewee must have federated reviews enabled.
federation.api_doc_endpoint_post_reviews_param_revi: Reviewer user ID (must belong to your tenant)
Reviewee user ID (must have federated reviews enabled)
federation.api_doc_endpoint_get_reviews_description: Get federated reviews for a specific user. Only returns approved reviews where the user has federated reviews enabled.
federation.api_doc_endpoint_get_reviews_param_user_: User ID to get reviews for
federation.api_doc_endpoint_get_transactions_id_des: Get the status and details of a specific federated transaction. Your tenant must be either the sender or receiver tenant.
federation.api_doc_endpoint_post_webhooks_test_desc: Verify HMAC signature correctness for webhook payloads. Tests that your signing implementation produces valid signatures.

shared.fit_intro: This area does four things: you choose which timebanks to partner with, decide what members can do together, set up any technical links to other software, and keep an eye on what happens.

settings.title: Start here
settings.summary: This page switches partnering on or off for your community and sets your basic rules. You do not add a partner here.
settings.fit: Use it for the main on/off switch, for whether other timebanks may ask to partner with you, and for how many partners you want at once. These choices apply to every partner.
settings.avoid: Passwords and keys from another system do not go here. They go on External platforms or Inbound API partners, under Technical setup.
settings.step_1_body: Do this only when your community is ready for other timebanks to see it.
settings.step_2_body: Choose whether other timebanks may send you requests, and the most partners you want.
settings.step_3_body: Save this page, then go to Partner directory to find a timebank and ask to partner.

partnerships.title: Your partner timebanks
partnerships.summary: A partnership is an agreement between your community and another timebank on this platform. Both sides have to agree before anything is shared.
partnerships.fit: Use this page to answer requests, to see who you are partnered with, to change what members can do together, and to pause or end a partnership.
partnerships.avoid: Timebanks that run on other software, such as TimeOverflow or Komunitin, are not set up here. They are under Technical setup.
partnerships.step_1_body: Pending means someone is waiting for an answer. Active means members can use what you agreed. Paused stops that without deleting anything.
partnerships.step_2_body: Profiles, messages, offers and requests, exchanges, events and groups can each be switched on or off. Share only what you both need.
partnerships.step_3_title: Agree a credit limit if you exchange.
partnerships.step_3_body: If members will exchange time with the partner, set up a credit agreement as well.

directory.title: Find a timebank to partner with
directory.summary: The directory lists other timebanks on this platform that have chosen to be found. From here you can ask one to partner with you.
directory.fit: Use this page to search for communities, read what they say about themselves, and send a request.
directory.avoid: Timebanks that run on other software are not listed here. They are set up under Technical setup.
directory.step_1_body: Use the region and topic filters to find communities that are a good fit.
directory.step_2_body: See what the community does and what it shares with partners before you ask.
directory.step_3_body: Say why you would like to partner and what you hope members will do together.

creditAgreements.title: Only needed when members exchange time with a partner
creditAgreements.summary: A credit agreement sets how many time credits can move between your community and a partner each month. Both sides have to approve it.
creditAgreements.fit: Use this page once you and a partner have agreed that your members may earn or spend time credits with each other.
creditAgreements.avoid: Sharing profiles or messages with a partner does not need a credit agreement. Leave exchanges switched off until you have one.
creditAgreements.step_1_body: Only timebanks you already have an active partnership with appear in the list.
creditAgreements.step_2_body: Agree with your partner the most credits that can move between you in a month.
creditAgreements.step_3_body: The Balances tab shows whether one community is giving much more than it receives.

externalPartners.title: Links to timebanks on other software
externalPartners.summary: This page connects your community to a timebank that runs on different software, such as TimeOverflow, Komunitin or Credit Commons, or on another NEXUS installation.
externalPartners.fit: Use it when this platform needs to contact the other system: you store its web address, choose which kind of system it is, and record how to sign in to it.
externalPartners.avoid: If another organisation's system needs to contact this platform, that is set up on Inbound API partners instead.
externalPartners.step_1_title: Choose the kind of system first.
externalPartners.step_1_body: Pick NEXUS, TimeOverflow, Komunitin or Credit Commons before the address. The choice decides what the address and keys mean.
externalPartners.step_2_title: Store only the keys it needs.
externalPartners.step_2_body: Fill in a key or secret only if that system asks for one. Leave the other fields empty.
externalPartners.step_3_title: Test before you switch it on.
externalPartners.step_3_body: Run the health check and read the log before you mark the partner active.

apiKeys.title: Keys that identify your community
apiKeys.summary: An API key is a long password that lets another system recognise requests from your community. Each partner link should have its own.
apiKeys.fit: Use this page to create, name and remove the keys used by your partner links.
apiKeys.avoid: Do not give these keys to an unrelated organisation. A system that needs to contact this platform gets its own sign-in on Inbound API partners.
apiKeys.step_1_title: Name the key after its purpose.
apiKeys.step_1_body: Include the partner and what it is for, so the next admin knows why it exists.
apiKeys.step_2_body: Tick only the permissions that link actually uses.
apiKeys.step_3_title: Remove keys you no longer use.
apiKeys.step_3_body: Remove a key straight away if it is unused or may have leaked, and check the partner has moved to the new one.

apiDocs.title: A reference for developers
apiDocs.summary: The developer guide explains how another system talks to this platform: signing in, the addresses to call, examples, errors and event messages. Nothing is set up on this page.
apiDocs.fit: Send a developer here when they need to understand how API keys, partner links and webhooks fit together.
apiDocs.avoid: You cannot create keys here. Use External platforms, API keys, Event webhooks or Inbound API partners, depending on which system contacts which.
apiDocs.step_1_body: It explains the difference between an API key and a webhook before the detail begins.
apiDocs.step_2_body: Authentication covers keys and signatures, Endpoints the addresses, Examples the data, and Webhooks the event messages.
apiDocs.step_3_title: Then go to the setup page.
apiDocs.step_3_body: After reading, go back to the page where that key or link is actually set up.

webhooks.title: Tell another system when something happens
webhooks.summary: A webhook is a message this platform sends to another system the moment something happens, such as a new message or exchange.
webhooks.fit: Use this page when a trusted partner's system needs to hear about events straight away.
webhooks.avoid: A webhook does not replace a partnership or a key. The system receiving it still has to be a partner you trust, with a shared signing secret.
webhooks.step_1_body: Use an https address that belongs to the partner receiving the messages.
webhooks.step_2_title: Choose only the events they need.
webhooks.step_2_body: Send as few kinds of event as possible.
webhooks.step_3_title: Test it and watch for failures.
webhooks.step_3_body: Send a test message, then check the delivery log so repeated failures are noticed.

creditCommons.title: Your community's place in a Credit Commons network
creditCommons.summary: Credit Commons is a way for separate timebank networks to keep accounts with each other. These settings describe your community within such a network. They have nothing to do with card payments.
creditCommons.fit: Use this page only if your community belongs to a Credit Commons network and has been given a name and settings to use.
creditCommons.avoid: Card payments, member subscriptions and sign-ins for other systems are not set up here.
creditCommons.step_1_title: Check your community's name in the network.
creditCommons.step_1_body: The short name and display name must match what the network agreed.
creditCommons.step_2_body: Enter the parent's address and short name only if your community sits under another one.
creditCommons.step_3_body: The validation window and the record check show whether your accounts match the rest of the network.

apiPartners.title: Sign-ins for systems that contact this platform
apiPartners.summary: This page is for outside systems that need to contact this platform, such as a council's system or a reporting tool that your community has approved.
apiPartners.fit: Use it to create a sign-in for such a system, limit what it may do and how often, try it in test mode, or suspend it.
apiPartners.avoid: A timebank on other software that this platform contacts is set up on External platforms, not here.
apiPartners.step_1_body: Enter the organisation and a contact email, so there is someone to speak to if the sign-in has to change.
apiPartners.step_2_title: Limit it before you share it.
apiPartners.step_2_body: Choose the fewest permissions, a request limit, the allowed addresses and test mode before you reveal the secret.
apiPartners.step_3_body: Pass it on safely, and create a new one if there is any doubt about who has seen it.

dataManagement.title: Export, import and clear partner records with care
dataManagement.summary: This page is for housekeeping of partner records. Partnerships, keys and links are not created here.
dataManagement.fit: Use it to export records, to try an import without changing anything, to import for real, and to clear old logs.
dataManagement.avoid: An import is not a way round approval. Partnerships and keys should still be checked on their own pages.
dataManagement.step_1_body: Run the preview so mistakes and duplicates show before anything changes.
dataManagement.step_2_title: Export only when you need to.
dataManagement.step_2_body: An export can contain sensitive details about partners. Keep the file safe.
dataManagement.step_3_body: Check how long your community has to keep these logs before you delete them.

activityFeed.title: What actually happened with your partners
activityFeed.summary: The activity feed is a timeline of everything that passed between your community and its partners.
activityFeed.fit: Use it to look into messages, exchanges, profile views, shared offers and requests, and changes to partnerships.
activityFeed.avoid: Nothing is set up here. It is a record to read and to help you find a problem.
activityFeed.step_1_body: Narrow the list to messages, exchanges, offers and requests, or partnership changes.
activityFeed.step_2_title: Check the direction and the partner.
activityFeed.step_2_body: Incoming and outgoing events tell different stories. Filter by partner when you are looking into one of them.
activityFeed.step_3_body: If the same thing keeps failing, go to the page for that partnership, key or webhook and put it right there.

analytics.title: See how partnering is going
analytics.summary: Analytics shows how much your partnerships are used and whether they are working.
analytics.fit: Use it to compare activity over time and between partners.
analytics.avoid: A healthy chart does not prove the sharing choices are right. Check those on Partnerships.
analytics.step_1_body: Watch for a jump in errors, a partner that has gone quiet, or unusual exchanges.
analytics.step_2_body: See whether a problem affects one partner or all of them.
analytics.step_3_body: Use Activity feed, Partnerships or Credit agreements to find the cause behind a number.

aggregates.title: Totals only, never individual members
aggregates.summary: Shared statistics are totals for your whole community, such as hours exchanged. They never contain an individual member's details.
aggregates.fit: Use this page when a national or regional network asks for summary figures from your community.
aggregates.avoid: This is not a way to pass members' personal details to anyone.
aggregates.step_1_title: Be clear why the figures are needed.
aggregates.step_1_body: For example a network's own reporting, a public report, or research your community has approved.
aggregates.step_2_body: Look at which totals are shared, and whether a very small number could point to one person.
aggregates.step_3_title: Check it is up to date.
aggregates.step_3_body: Use the dates shown to confirm the figures reflect recent activity.

meta.title: Federation aggregates
meta.description: Share anonymised community statistics with partner networks and control the signed public feed.

consent.title: Aggregate sharing consent
consent.endpoint_prefix: When enabled, the signed public feed at
consent.endpoint_suffix: returns anonymised monthly aggregates to partner networks.
